findings.title: Pause and Delete actions never render when the menu is used with promRule only (list view)
findings.body: The PR makes `AlertRuleMenu` usable with only a `promRule` from the new list view, and adds `grafanaPauseAbility`/`grafanaDeleteAbility` so `canPause`/`canDelete` can become true in that case. However both menu items are still gated on a `rulerRule`: the pause item at line 123 requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` and the delete item at line 165 requires `rulerRule && ...`. The new list components (`GrafanaGroupLoader` and `FilterView`) render `GrafanaRuleListItem` -> `RuleActionsButtons.V2` with only `promRule` and never pass a `rulerRule`, so `rulerRule` is always undefined there. As a result, in the new (prom-only) list view the user can no longer Pause or Delete a rule even when the computed `canPause`/`canDelete` (from the Grafana prom abilities) are true and `handleDelete` is wired up. The `canPause`/`canDelete` computations and `handleDelete` prop are effectively dead in that view. Either drop the `rulerRule` guards (the delete handler and `MenuItemPauseRule` should use the prom rule / identifier) or stop computing those abilities for prom-only consumers.

findings.title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable after delegating to useAllRulerRuleAbilities
findings.body: Before this change `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` from the `CombinedRule` group and used it to mark federated rule groups as immutable (no Edit/Delete/Pause). The new implementation delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `isFederated = false` (line 245, with a `// TODO: Add support for federated rules` comment) because a `RulerRuleDTO` alone does not carry the group's `source_tenants`. Any component still consuming `useAlertRuleAbility`/`useAlertRuleAbilities` (e.g. RuleDetails) will therefore show Edit/Delete/Pause affordances for federated Mimir rule groups, which are read-only, leading to actions that the backend rejects. The federation check needs to be preserved (pass the group or the federated flag through to the ruler-abilities hook).

findings.title: Missing React `key` on GrafanaRuleListItem in the rule list map
findings.body: In the `switch (origin)` inside `rules.map(...)` the `grafana` branch renders `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` without a `key`, even though the loop destructures `key` from `ruleWithOrigin` and the `datasource`/`default` branches both pass `key={key}`. This triggers the React "each child in a list should have a unique key" warning and forces index-based reconciliation for these rows, whose children (`RuleActionsButtons`) hold per-row state (silence drawer, clone redirect). It should pass `key={key}` like the other branches.

findings.title: View link no longer carries returnTo, breaking back-navigation from the rule view
findings.body: The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader`'s `GrafanaRuleListItem` built the view URL with `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo: createReturnTo() })`. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem` builds it as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo`, so navigating from the list into a rule and pressing the "back" control in the rule viewer will no longer return the user to the list/filter they came from. This is a behavior regression from the previous implementation.

findings.title: Stale comment/variable name referencing ruler preloading that was removed
findings.body: The ruler `prefetch` call was removed from `getGroupsAndProvideCache`, but the surrounding comment still says "This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX" and the local variable is still named `cacheAndRulerPreload`. Since only Prometheus groups are cached now, the comment and name are misleading about what the code does and should be updated to reflect that only the Prometheus group cache is being warmed.
